subject: physics
title: Lenses
key_idea: A converging lens focuses parallel rays at its principal focus; a diverging lens spreads them. Lens power is 1 / f, and 1/u + 1/v = 1/f locates the image. Real images can be projected; virtual images cannot.

blocks.text: A lens changes the direction of light by refraction at its two curved surfaces. The two types do opposite jobs.

items.meaning: A lens, thicker in the middle, that brings parallel rays to a point called the principal focus.
A lens, thinner in the middle, that spreads parallel rays so they seem to come from a point behind the lens.
The distance from the centre of the lens to the principal focus.
A measure of how strongly a lens bends light. It is 1 / f.

items: A converging lens has a real principal focus on the far side. Its focal length is positive.
A diverging lens has a virtual principal focus on the same side as the incoming light. Its focal length is negative.
A short focal length means a powerful lens.
One dioptre is a power of 1 m⁻¹. A lens of focal length 0.25 m has power +4.0 D.

blocks.label: Thin lenses in contact
where: P₁, P₂, P₃ = powers of the separate lenses (D)

blocks.text: Powers add for thin lenses placed together. A diverging lens contributes a negative power.

items: P = 1 / f, with f in metres.
Powers of thin lenses in contact add.

blocks.text: A ray diagram locates the image of one point on an object. Draw two of these three rays from the top of the object. Where they meet is the image of that point.

items.text: A ray parallel to the axis is refracted through the principal focus (converging lens).
A ray through the centre of the lens goes straight on.
A ray through the principal focus on the object side leaves parallel to the axis.

items.meaning: An image formed where rays actually meet. It can be shown on a screen.
An image formed where rays only appear to come from. It cannot be shown on a screen.

rows: Virtual, upright, larger, on the same side as the object

items: A diverging lens always gives a virtual, upright, smaller image, closer to the lens than the object.
A magnifying glass is a converging lens with the object inside the focal length.
A real image can be projected onto a screen; a virtual image cannot.
Inside the focal length, a converging lens gives a virtual, magnified image.

blocks.text: The lens equation links the object distance u, image distance v and focal length f. Use the real-is-positive convention.

blocks.label: Thin lens equation
where: u = object distance from the lens (m)
v = image distance from the lens (m)

items: Distances to real objects and real images are positive.
f is positive for a converging lens and negative for a diverging lens.
A negative v means a virtual image, on the same side as the object.

blocks.label: Magnification
blocks.formula: m = image height / object height = v / u

items: The size of m is what matters: m > 1 means a magnified image, m < 1 a diminished one.
With the real-is-positive convention, v is negative for a virtual image, so v / u is negative.

diagram.alt: Use the lens equation to find an image distance.
diagram.question: An object is {u} cm from a converging lens of focal length {f} cm. Calculate the image distance.

items: m = v / u = image height ÷ object height.

checks.q: A converging lens has a focal length of 20 cm. Calculate its power.
An object is 30 cm from a converging lens of focal length 10 cm. Calculate the image distance and the magnification.
State the difference between a real image and a virtual image.
checks.a: A real image is formed where rays actually meet and can be shown on a screen. A virtual image is where rays only seem to come from and cannot be shown on a screen.
